solves: Takes a short code of known length, sent by SMS or e-mail, with one cell per character, to confirm access.
use_when: To confirm access with a code sent by SMS or e-mail: length 6 or 4, by the length of the code.
On a touch screen, where the code is usually typed on the phone: size large; on other screens, size default.
When the code is typed in a public place: masked.
For a code with letters and numbers, such as A7K2Q9: the field takes it and the cell does not change.
do_not_use_when: For free one-line text: use nph-input.
Without nph-field: the label, the help and the error belong to nph-field.
With cells of different sizes: use the same size in the whole field.
To paint the resend action with a loose color: the resend is an nph-button below the field, with the label in color/link.

length.constraint: The number of cells, the Figma property of the set. Any other value draws nothing and emits console.error in development. A shorter length cuts the current value.

size.constraint: default draws cells of control/height-default and large of control/height-large, for touch screens. The same in every cell. Any other value draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

invalid.constraint: The error state of the Figma set: every cell takes the border status/error and the inner input gets aria-invalid. The error sentence belongs to nph-field. disabled wins.

disabled.constraint: The disabled state of the Figma set: out of the Tab order, background color/muted and the whole field at state/disabled-opacity. A disabled fieldset does the same and takes the value out of the form data. It wins over invalid.

masked.constraint: The Figma cell property that hides the character, on the host because the cells are not public: every filled cell shows a dot in place of the character. The mask is visual only: the input stays a text input and a screen reader reads the code.

required.constraint: Announced as aria-required on the inner input. There is no constraint validation: the error sentence belongs to nph-field.

name.constraint: The name of the entry in the form data. It reflects, because the form reads the attribute of the host; without it, the field adds nothing to the form data.

value.constraint: The code: only ASCII letters and digits, up to length, with the case as typed. The value attribute is the initial value and the value of form reset; the property is the current value. A value set from code with other characters or longer than length is cleaned, cut and reported with console.warn in development. Setting it from code never fires an event.

label.constraint: The accessible name, as text, never shown. nph-field writes it. A label associated with the host names the field first; label is the name when there is none. With no name at all, the field renders and warns once in development.

description.constraint: The accessible description, as text: the help or the error sentence that nph-field writes. It goes into an inner element hidden by clipping, referenced by aria-describedby.

input.constraint: The native input event of the inner input, which crosses the shadow root with the host as its target, once per change the person makes, with the value already cleaned. A dropped character fires nothing.

change.constraint: Fired by the host, bubbling, when the person leaves the field or presses Enter with a value different from the one at focus.

length.choose_when: 6 is the default. 4 for a four-character code.

size.choose_when: default (36 px) on most screens. large (44 px) on a touch screen, where the code is usually typed on the phone.
do_not_combine_with: cells of different sizes in the same field.

masked.choose_when: Only when the code is typed in a public place; elsewhere seeing the character helps the person check it.

default.changes_for_user: The empty cells wait for the code.

hover.changes_for_user: Every cell border darkens while the pointer is over the field, which is one target. Error and disabled keep their border.

focus.changes_for_user: The cell where the next character goes, the active cell, takes the focus border and a halo outside it, out of the layout. With the code full, it is the last cell.

error.changes_for_user: Every cell takes the error border; the sentence is written by nph-field.

error_focus.changes_for_user: The active cell keeps the error border and the halo turns to the error tone.

disabled.changes_for_user: The field cannot be focused or edited and is drawn lighter, on the muted background.

business_rules: The field takes only ASCII letters and digits; any other character typed is dropped and fires nothing.
A pasted code is cleaned and replaces the whole value, cut at length; a paste with no letter or digit changes nothing.
Focus puts the caret on the next empty cell; a click on a cell puts the caret on it, or at the end of the code.
Enter submits the form that owns the field, through its default button, or the form itself with none; a disabled default button stops it, and a consumer that cancels Enter keeps the form.
Setting value from code never fires input or change.
The value attribute is the initial value and the reset value; once the person or the code changes the value, a new value attribute does not replace it.
domain_errors: invalid: a wrong or expired code. Every cell shows the error border; nph-field writes the sentence and passes it as description.

tokens.cell: color/background background, color/input border at border/width, radius/control
tokens.cell_size: control/height-default or control/height-large, as width and height

ai_hints: Use nph-input-otp for a short code of known length sent by SMS or e-mail; for free text, use nph-input.
Put it in an nph-field, which writes label, description, invalid and required.
Set length to the length of the code; 6 is the default.
Use size large on a touch screen and the same size in the whole field.
Set masked only when the code is typed in a public place.
Give it a name inside a form; read the code from value on input or change.
Put the resend action below the field, as a separate nph-button; it is not part of the field.

accessibility.semantics: One native text input inside the shadow root, laid over the cells. The cells only draw and are aria-hidden: the code is one value, with one name.
accessibility.accessible_name: The label of nph-field, written as label. A label associated with the host names the inner input first, by element reference. With no name, the field renders and warns in development.
keyboard: Tab enters and leaves the field: one stop for the whole code.
Typing fills the active cell and moves to the next one.
Backspace removes the character before the caret.
Arrow Left, Arrow Right, Home and End move the active cell.
Enter submits the form that owns the field.
accessibility.focus: The active cell shows the focus border and the halo, outside the cell and out of the layout; space/inline is wider than the halo, so a neighbor never covers it.
accessibility.contrast: The character and the dot use color/foreground, at least 4.5:1 on color/background; the border color/input and the error border status/error are at least 3:1, in light and dark in every brand. The disabled state has no minimum contrast.
accessibility.color_alternative: The error always comes with the sentence of nph-field, read as the description; disabled combines opacity with the muted background.

invalid_combinations: A length other than 6 or 4 — the field draws nothing.
A size other than default or large — the field draws nothing.
masked together with a visible character — not possible: masked replaces every character by the dot.
disabled with invalid — disabled wins: no error border and no aria-invalid.
anti_patterns: Leaving the field without nph-field, with no label, help or error.
Showing the dot and the character at the same time.
Painting the resend action with a loose color instead of color/link.
Using it for free text, where nph-input is the choice.
Using it for a code whose length is not known in advance.
